questions.q: Which Roman figure did George Washington try to emulate?
a: Cato, known for virtue and resistance to corruption
Cicero, admired mainly for his speeches in the senate
Caesar, celebrated for expanding Rome's territory
Augustus, remembered for building a lasting empire
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Washington identified with Cato's virtue and opposition to aristocratic power.

questions.q: Which Greek philosopher particularly shaped Jefferson's thinking?
a: Epicurus
Plato
Aristotle
Socrates
questions.why: Lesson 2 links Epicurus's vision of life to the pursuit of happiness in the Declaration.

questions.q: What did the founders want ancient models to help America achieve?
a: A strong military and an educated public capable of reasoned decisions
A monarchy modeled on the Roman emperors
A trading empire that could rival Britain economically
A religious state guided by classical mythology
questions.why: Lesson 2 says they sought a republic that could withstand future European threats.

questions.q: What happened to classicism in nineteenth-century America?
a: It faded as Romanticism and more rational views gained ground
It became the official philosophy of the federal government
It was revived by a new generation of founders
It was replaced entirely by religious doctrine
questions.why: Lesson 3 says virtue stopped guiding every endeavor as freedom for all took priority.

questions.q: What did Washington do with the Roman generals Fabius and Cincinnatus?
a: He studied their strategies and imitated them against the British
He wrote a book comparing their leadership styles
He named two new states after them
He rejected their tactics as unsuited to America
questions.why: Lesson 1 says he learned from their methods and nearly impersonated them.
